title: live_switch kwarg path mis-indexes when an upstream frame is absent from dfs_by_name
description: In the kwarg branch, `dfs = tuple(dfs_by_name[name] for name in input_names if name in dfs_by_name)` compacts to only the present names, but the selection loop later indexes the compacted tuple using the position of the matching name within the FULL input_names list: `for i, name in enumerate(input_names): if name == inp: return dfs[i]`. If any earlier input name is missing from dfs_by_name, `i` is offset relative to the compacted `dfs`, so the wrong frame is returned (or IndexError when i >= len(dfs)). The executor itself always calls the function positionally (_execute_lazy.py:1206 `fn(*input_lfs)` and :1856 `result = fn(*input_lfs)`), so this path is only reached by direct kwarg callers (tests/future callers) -- hence the low real-world severity -- but the kwarg contract is silently wrong. The index should be computed against the same filtered name list used to build `dfs`.
evidence: Builder l.645 filters names present in dfs_by_name; l.651-653 indexes dfs by position in unfiltered input_names. Executor passes positional args only (_execute_lazy.py:1206, 1856), so the kwarg branch is exercised solely by direct callers.
